title: Separable-closure Cech nerve, profinite test points and vertex-coordinate predicate
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Omega/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], with both fields in a common universe $u$. Write $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(\Omega)$ with its Krull topology. In the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-scheme], let $U$ be the actual object $v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ induced by the structure embedding, and let $a:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be its arrow to the final object. Define $W_q$ for $q\geq0$ as the degree-$q$ object of the Cech nerve of $a$, namely the $(q+1)$-fold fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $U$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with vertex projections $p_j:W_q\to U$ for $0\leq j\leq q$. Define the profinite space $P_q=G^{\{0,\ldots,q-1\}}$, including the singleton $P_0$. For $g\in P_q$ and any $j\in\mathbb N$, put $h_j(g)$ equal to the ordered product of the first $\min(j,q)$ entries of $g$, with empty product $1$. For the profinite test object $\Omega[P_q]=\operatorname{Spec}LC(P_q,\mathbb Z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], let $t_g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\Omega[P_q]$ be the point whose first component is induced by $LC(P_q,\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_g}\mathbb Z\to\Omega$ and whose second component is the identity. For a family of scheme isomorphisms $e_q:W_q\simeq\Omega[P_q]$, define $\operatorname{AreCoordinates}(e)$ to mean that $p_0\circ e_q^{-1}$ is the structural projection $\Omega[P_q]\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for every $q$, and that $p_j\circ e_q^{-1}\circ t_g=\operatorname{Spec}(h_j(g))$ for every $q$, $g\in P_q$ and $0\leq j\leq q$. This defines the nerve, test points and coordinate predicate, and does not assert existence of such isomorphisms.
